body.text: How do you reach Fethiye from Dalaman Airport (DLM)?

Dalaman Airport (DLM) sits roughly 48 to 50 kilometres northwest of central Fethiye—a straightforward 45-to-60-minute drive along the coastal D400 highway via Göcek, as noted by [Dalaman Airport Transfer](https://www.dalamanairporttransfer.com/en/blog/dalaman-airport-fethiye-transfer). Add another 20 to 25 minutes over the pine ridge if you are staying directly in Ölüdeniz, Hisarönü, or Kayaköy.

Budget travellers can board the municipal [MUTTAŞ Line 48-25 airport bus](https://ulasim.muttas.com.tr/hat/48-25-fethiye-otogar-dalaman-havalimani-439) or HAVAŞ shuttle directly outside the terminal (credit cards are accepted on MUTTAŞ buses). Both buses terminate at Fethiye Otogar (the main bus station), where you switch to a local dolmuş minibus for Ölüdeniz, Çalış Beach, or Kayaköy. For families, groups of three or more, or late-night flights, pre-booking a private transfer or picking up a rental car at DLM eliminates the Otogar connection and drops you straight at your hotel door.
Is Babadağ paragliding safe and how much does it cost?

Tandem paragliding from Babadağ Mountain is tightly regulated and has a strong safety record when you fly with a licensed, insured commercial pilot rather than chasing the cheapest street tout. In 2026, expect to pay roughly $130 to $160 USD per flight, with transparent operators such as [Atmos Paragliding](https://www.atmosparagliding.com/blog/paragliding-oludeniz-price-2026-real-costs) quoting $150 all-inclusive for transfer, mountain entry, and photos/video.

Pilots launch from graded runways at 1,200 m, 1,700 m, 1,800 m, and 1,960 m depending on wind direction, gliding 25 to 35 minutes down to Belcekız Beach. Non-fliers can ride the [Babadağ Teleferik cable car](https://www.babadagteleferik.com.tr/en/teleferik/) from the 226-metre main station up to the summit restaurants for the same panoramic lagoon view—2026 round-trip cable car fares are 890 TL for adults and 660 TL for students ([Dragon Paragliding](https://dragonparagliding.com/en/blog/babadag-cable-car-prices-2026/)). Before booking any flight, follow four safety checks:

items: Confirm pilot certification: Verify your pilot holds a current Turkish Aeronautical Association (THK) T2 commercial tandem licence and passenger insurance.
Check what the quote includes: Ask upfront whether the cable car or mountain shuttle, national park fee, and GoPro/360 video package are bundled or charged separately.
Respect weather calls: Reputable operators delay or cancel flights when crosswinds spike; never pressure a pilot to launch in marginal conditions.
Book early morning for smoother air: The 08:30–10:30 slots bring calmer air and softer light over the lagoon, while late afternoon suits sunset flights.

body.text: What is the story behind Kayaköy Ghost Town?

Kayaköy (historically Levissi) is an abandoned hillside settlement of 350 to 400 two-storey stone houses, two churches, a school, and rainwater cisterns just 8 kilometres south of Fethiye, documented by [Turkish Museums](https://turkishmuseums.com/museum/detail/2187-mugla-kayakoy-archaeological-site/2187/4). Once home to a prosperous Anatolian Greek community, the village was emptied during the 1923 population exchange between Greece and Türkiye and further damaged by the 1957 Fethiye earthquake.

As described in [GoTürkiye's Kayaköy feature](https://goturkiye.com/blog/the-ghost-town-fethiyes-kayakoy-village), every house was built without blocking its neighbour's sunlight or valley view. Foreign visitors pay €3 at the gate (check seasonal hours on muze.gov.tr). Give yourself 90 minutes to climb the stone paths to the upper church, then stay in the modern village below for a garden lunch—or hike the marked 6-kilometre Lycian Way footpath through pine forest directly from Kayaköy down to Ölüdeniz Lagoon.
Which Fethiye bays are quieter than Ölüdeniz beach?

Ölüdeniz's Kumburnu Nature Park lagoon (85 TL per person or 255 TL per car in 2026, per [viravira.co's 2026 Fethiye bay guide](https://www.viravira.co/tr/yatcilik/fethiyenin-en-guzel-koylari-ve-plajlari/)) fills by 10:30 in July and August. Driving 10 to 35 minutes out of the lagoon basin opens up far calmer pine-shaded coves with equally clear water.

faq.q: Should you stay in Fethiye town, Çalış Beach, or Ölüdeniz?
faq.a: Stay in Fethiye's Karagözler or Paspatur harbour area for authentic dining and boat departures, Çalış Beach for flat sunset walks and budget-friendly hotels, or Kayaköy/Faralya for quiet boutique stays away from Hisarönü's nightlife strip.

faq.q: Is there a weight or age limit for Babadağ paragliding?
faq.a: Most licensed operators fly passengers from roughly age 5–6 upwards and up to 100–110 kg depending on wind conditions and harness sizing; confirm exact limits when booking.

faq.q: Can you drive down to Butterfly Valley?
faq.a: No road reaches the beach at Butterfly Valley. You can view the canyon from the clifftop road near Faralya, or reach the shore by water taxi or day boat from Belcekız Beach in Ölüdeniz.

faq.q: How long does the hike from Kayaköy to Ölüdeniz take?
faq.a: The rocky coastal footpath—part of the Lycian Way—takes about 1.5 to 2 hours downhill from Kayaköy to Ölüdeniz Lagoon. Wear sturdy shoes and start early to avoid midday heat.

faq.q: What is the difference between Belcekız Beach and Ölüdeniz Lagoon?
faq.a: Belcekız is the wide, open-sea pebble beach where paragliders land (free entry; sunbeds extra), while Kumburnu Lagoon is the sheltered, flat-water sandspit inside the paid Ölüdeniz–Kıdrak Nature Park.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Fethiye and Ölüdeniz?
faq.a: May to mid-June and mid-September through October offer warm 24–29°C days, reliable paragliding thermals, swimmable seas, and far quieter bays than July and August.
